title: Hurricane or tropical storm
summary: Henrico is inland, but wind, flooding and tornadoes reach this far.

items.text: Know the terms: a **watch** means a storm is possible within 48 hours. A **warning** means it is expected within 36 hours.
items.note: On a watch, monitor NOAA Weather Radio, local media and alerts, and gather supplies in case you lose power. On a warning, finish preparing and leave if officials direct you to. If no evacuation is ordered, shelter in place.

items.text: Use several alert methods: the FEMA app, community alerts, and Emergency Alert System and Wireless Emergency Alert messages.
items.note: EAS and WEA messages need no sign-up.

items.text: Learn about evacuation. Know Your Zone covers coastal Virginia, so follow Henrico officials' instructions.
Decide now whether we are going to Gram's.
items.note: Leave early enough to avoid being trapped by severe weather.

items.text: Keep your phone charged, and have backup charging devices.
Stock supplies for the household: medication, disinfectant and pet supplies.
items.note: You may go days or weeks without access to stores or services.

items.text: Check the insulin supply and the T1D go-kit.
Pets: at least 3 days of food, water and medicine.
Update insurance and ID, with digital copies in a password-protected space.
Bring in patio furniture, trash cans, bikes and toys. Clear gutters and drains.
Anchor gas grills and propane tanks.
Photograph or video your home's condition for insurance.
Keep portable generators outdoors, at least 20 feet from the house, protected from moisture.
Monitor emergency alerts.
If officials order an evacuation for your zone, **leave immediately**.
In high wind, take refuge in a designated storm shelter or an interior room.
items.note: Tornadoes can spin off from a hurricane.

items.text: If floodwater traps you, go to the highest level. **Do not go into a closed attic.**
**Never walk, swim or drive through floodwater.**
items.note: 6 inches of fast-moving water can knock you down. 1 foot can sweep away a vehicle.

items.text: Generators stay outdoors, at least 20 feet from the house.
Follow local officials. Wait to return until they say the area is safe.
Stay out of floodwater.
items.note: It can carry germs, debris, chemicals and waste, and downed or underground power lines can electrify it.

items.text: Do not enter buildings until they have been inspected for electrical, gas, septic and water problems.
Do not drink tap water until it is confirmed safe. Boil or purify it if unsure.
Stay at least 30 feet from downed power lines, treat them as live, and report them to the utility.
Do not touch wet electrical equipment or anything while standing in water. If it is safe, turn off power at the main breaker.
For cleanup, wear protective clothing, work with a partner, and wear a mask for mold or debris. Children should not help.
Save phone calls for emergencies. Text instead.
Photograph any damage and contact your insurance company.
If the power was out, check food and refrigerated medicine.
